answer: Each identity posts a 40-credit saffron bond and must pass a peer challenge window for its seal. Auditors wander the register unpredictably, so bulk fakes cannot hide. A challenger stakes 10 credits to dispute an identity; the owner must answer with a fresh work proof, or the bond burns. Each fake also pays 30 plus 5 per earlier fake, so the 1,000th costs 5,025 and 1,000 fakes lock 40,000 plus 2,527,500. Rented defence fails: the proof must carry its own key and match its velvet entry, and a borrowed proof burns both bonds. An honest agent posts 40 once.
